items.t: The usual duplex form: Both municipalities carry the two-unit form in their residential frameworks (City Zoning 6700; District Zoning 3210) and both sit inside the provincial SSMUH framework, so North Vancouver's duplex form class is individual duplex buildings on single lots built under the zoning of their day, in either municipality.

faq.q: Can I buy just one side of a duplex in North Vancouver?
faq.a: Only if that side is legally separate — a strata lot in a 2-lot strata plan, or its own fee-simple lot from a subdivision. None is verified by name at the city-wide level; a single-lot duplex sells whole. Check the title first.

faq.q: Which municipality's rules apply to my lot — City or District?
faq.a: The two frames are never interchanged, and the City's servicing Bylaw 8014 is never a District position.

No. It is two municipalities — the District of North Vancouver, governed District-wide by OCP Bylaw 7900, and the City of North Vancouver, guided by OCP Bylaw, 2014, No. 8400 — with separate councils, bylaws and taxes.

faq.q: How do residents reach downtown Vancouver without a car?
faq.a: The SeaBus sails from Lonsdale Quay at the foot of Lonsdale Avenue to Waterfront Station in Vancouver, and buses meet the ferry at the Lonsdale Quay exchange.

faq.q: Which school district serves North Vancouver, and how do catchments work?
faq.a: School District 44 serves both municipalities, with no middle tier (elementary K–7, secondary 8–12). Catchments are address-based and must be confirmed with the district for the exact address.
